Owner: ScalaFIM surface-view-javafx, shared lighting contracts as appropriate.
Consumer: plsneuro E4.9 bd-01M1SC71551W831TM99XD0GQFV (foreign-store provenance).
Observed on local JavaFX24/JDK25/macOS: NativeStudyProbe renders a four-vertex fixture with SurfaceLighting.Default nearly black despite light signed-loading colors; same geometry/camera/data renders visible orange/gray with SurfaceLighting.Unlit. Artifacts: /private/tmp/plsneuro-surface-ui.png.surface.png (lit), /private/tmp/plsneuro-surface-ui-unlit.png.surface.png (unlit). Geometry/manifest: /private/tmp/plsneuro-surface-ui-unlit.png.surface-resource/resource.json and lh.white/pial.surf.gii. Probe source: /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/scala/plsneuro/modules/desktop/src/test/scala/plsneuro/desktop/NativeStudyProbe.scala; result host ResultSurfaceView.scala. Default->Unlit is the only presentation policy change between these specimens. This is a reproduced visual discrepancy, not yet a proved cause.
Source inspection: JavaFxSurfaceProgram.materialMode collapses Directional into Lit; configureMaterial sets diffuse texture and relies on JavaFX lighting. Investigate whether ambient/diffuse/direction in SurfaceLighting are honored and whether auto-light placement interacts with normalized mesh layout/camera. Do not tune only the tiny fixture or waive the declared lighting contract.
Acceptance: minimal native reproduction plus asymmetric lit/unlit expected-color evidence; exercise multiple physical mesh scales, camera/orbit, declared ambient/diffuse/direction, and real cortical fixture. Compare backend-neutral reference/raster expectations with native output. Preserve explicit unlit quantitative colors. Native/provider tests and downstream visual review required before claiming repaired. Current plsneuro selects labeled Unlit for result colors; shaded lighting remains unresolved.
set.title: Investigate nearly black JavaFX lit surfaces and declared lighting fidelity
